stories.headline: Legendary Singer S Janaki, the Nightingale of South India, Dies at 88
stories.what: S Janaki, one of the most celebrated playback singers in Indian cinema and widely known as the Nightingale of South India, passed away at the age of 88 in Mysuru due to age-related ailments. Her voice defined generations of Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam cinema, spanning a career of over six decades. Tributes poured in from across the film world, with luminaries including Rajinikanth, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, and Kamal Haasan expressing grief at her passing.
stories.lens: S Janaki's voice was the soundtrack to the childhoods and memories of hundreds of millions of Indians across southern states — her death marks the end of a truly irreplaceable era in Indian music.
stories.article:
S Janaki, the legendary playback singer revered across South India as the Nightingale of the South, passed away at the age of 88 in Mysuru, succumbing to age-related ailments. Her death marks the end of one of the most extraordinary careers in Indian film music, a voice that graced films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and several other languages over more than six decades.

The news triggered an immediate outpouring of grief from the who's who of Indian cinema and public life. Rajinikanth, Kamal Haasan, and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay were among the first to pay tribute, reflecting the depth of her cultural footprint across the southern states. For audiences across generations, her voice was inseparable from some of the most beloved film songs ever recorded in Indian cinema.

Janaki's range and versatility were the hallmark of her artistry — she could move effortlessly from devotional songs to peppy numbers to soul-stirring romantic ballads, lending each a warmth and expressiveness that made her irreplaceable. She had received numerous national and state awards over the years and remained a deeply respected figure in the Indian music world well into her final years.

Her passing leaves a void in Indian playback singing that is near impossible to fill. Fans, musicians, and film personalities across the country are mourning not just the loss of a singer, but the end of an era — one in which the human voice, unaided by modern production excess, carried entire films on its shoulders.
key_facts: S Janaki passed away at age 88 in Mysuru
Cause of death: age-related ailments
Known as the Nightingale of South India
Tributes from Rajinikanth, CM Vijay, Kamal Haasan and others

stories.headline: Sohail Khan Opens Up on Divorce from Seema Sajdeh: 'Wasn't in the Right Frame of Mind'
stories.what: Actor Sohail Khan has spoken candidly about his divorce from Seema Sajdeh, admitting that he was not in the right frame of mind during the period that led to the breakdown of their marriage. The couple's split had played out partly in public view through the reality show that featured Seema Sajdeh, making their personal journey a subject of widespread discussion. Sohail's remarks are among the most direct he has made on the matter.
stories.lens: Bollywood separations rarely come with this level of personal candour from the quieter party — Sohail Khan's admission offers a rare, unfiltered look behind the curtain of a high-profile celebrity marriage.
stories.article:
Sohail Khan has broken his relative silence on his divorce from Seema Sajdeh, saying he was not in the right frame of mind during the critical period of their relationship. The actor, younger brother of Salman Khan, made the candid admission in a recent interview, offering one of the most personal accounts he has given of the marital breakdown.

The separation of Sohail and Seema had been a subject of public discussion partly because Seema Sajdeh appeared in the reality series 'Fabulous Lives of Bollywood Wives', where aspects of her post-marriage life played out on screen. For much of that time, Sohail had stayed largely out of the spotlight on the issue.

His acknowledgment that he was not mentally in the right place during this phase suggests a degree of self-reflection that is uncommon in public discourse around celebrity divorces in India. It also humanises a narrative that had, until now, been seen mostly from one vantage point.

The interview is likely to reignite interest in the couple's story, which remains one of the more closely watched personal sagas in Bollywood's recent memory. Both Sohail and Seema have since moved on with their respective lives and work.
key_facts: Sohail Khan admits he was 'not in the right frame of mind' during divorce
He was married to Seema Sajdeh
Seema featured in reality show Fabulous Lives of Bollywood Wives

Anshula Kapoor offered fans a belated but delightful look inside her wedding reception, sharing a series of previously unseen photographs from the celebration. The images capture the joyous energy of the event, with none of the studied formality of official shoot pictures.

stories.headline: Anjali Anand Says Her Role in 'Bell Bottom' Was Purely So 'a Terrorist Could Fall on Top of Me'
stories.what: Actress Anjali Anand has made a sharp, self-deprecating observation about her role in the Akshay Kumar-starrer 'Bell Bottom', saying she was cast in the film only so that a terrorist could fall on top of her — pointedly critiquing the nature of the role she was given. The candid remark throws light on the often superficial parts that supporting actresses are offered in mainstream Bollywood action films.
stories.lens: Anjali Anand's blunt, witty critique cuts to a real and persistent issue in Hindi cinema — the tokenism of female roles in action blockbusters — and her willingness to name it publicly is notable.
stories.article:
Anjali Anand has delivered one of Bollywood's more pointed pieces of self-critique in recent memory, saying that her entire presence in the Akshay Kumar action film 'Bell Bottom' amounted to little more than being someone a terrorist could fall on top of. The remark, made with evident dry wit, is a sharp commentary on the quality of roles available to supporting actresses in mainstream Hindi commercial cinema.

'Bell Bottom', released in 2021, was a period action thriller set against the backdrop of an airline hijacking. While the film featured a strong central role for Akshay Kumar, Anjali Anand's observation suggests her own part was purely functional — a prop to the action rather than a character with agency.

Her candour is striking because actresses in Bollywood, particularly those at a mid-level in the industry, rarely speak so directly about the inadequacy of their own roles. The comment implicitly critiques both the writers and directors who reduce female characters to set-dressing in action blockbusters and the industry norms that make such casting routine.

Anjali Anand, who has been more prominent in web series and comedic work, appears to be using the platform of her current press rounds to be refreshingly direct about the realities of working in commercial Hindi films. Her words are likely to resonate with audiences and fellow actors who have long noticed the same pattern.
key_facts: Anjali Anand says she was in Bell Bottom only for a terrorist to fall on her
Bell Bottom starred Akshay Kumar
Remark critiques superficial female roles in Bollywood action films
